name: Smog
label: Drag City
lede: One man, a secondhand four-track and a name he later decided was ugly: seventeen years of Bill Callahan getting from out-of-tune hiss to some of the plainest, deadliest songs in American indie.

eras.title: The dumpster Portastudio
eras.text: Bill Callahan, a Maryland kid whose parents were language analysts for the National Security Agency, started Smog alone with cheap tape machines and a guitar he was still learning. He wasn't going for lo-fi as a style; four-track cassettes were what he could afford.

years.h: Macrame Gunplay: Smog's first cassette, on Bill Callahan's own Disaster label
years.p: A sparse, primitive tape-only release. Bill Callahan put out his early Smog cassettes himself under the name Disaster.

years.h: Sewn to the Sky, recorded on a "dumpster Portastudio"
years.p: Smog's first LP, on Disaster, was taped in Georgia and Maryland on what the liner notes call a dumpster Portastudio. Mostly instrumental, noisy and badly tuned.
years.xp:
Spin said Bill Callahan was relishing the process with little regard for form, or for the guitar he was still learning to play. Trouser Press called the album primitive and promising.

Drag City later reissued it, on CD in November 1995 and LP in January 1996.

years.h: Floating EP: Smog's first Drag City record
years.p: Drag City catalog number 6, a 7-inch. Its song "Red Apples" resurfaces six years later on Red Apple Falls, and [[Cat Power|05755bf1-380c-487f-983f-d1a02401fa28]] covers it on The Covers Record.

eras.title: Hiss for Drag City
eras.text: With Drag City behind him, Bill Callahan put out a record nearly every year and the melodies started to show through the noise. AllMusic files these records under the home-recording boom, songs full of childhood memories, failed relationships and dashed hopes.

years.h: Forgotten Foundation, Smog's first album for Drag City
years.p: Drag City No. 13. Bill Callahan adds melody to the four-track murk without cleaning it up.

years.h: Julius Caesar: Smog songs, still raw, starting to land
years.p: Bill Callahan's third LP, Drag City No. 31. Cynthia Dall, then his girlfriend, sings on Smog records in these years, and he on hers.

years.h: Burning Kingdom EP
years.p: A Drag City EP (No. 41), issued on 12-inch, cassette and CD.

years.h: Wild Love, the last of Smog's home-taped years
years.p: Bill Callahan's fourth album, still home-recorded, still Drag City. The same year Drag City reissues Sewn to the Sky.

eras.title: Jim O'Rourke opens the door
eras.text: Recording with Jim O'Rourke gave Bill Callahan an engineer who actually liked his songs, and the records got bigger: organ, strings, drums, a children's choir. Meanwhile his life moved around the country, from a South Carolina farmhouse to Chicago.

years.h: Kicking a Couple Around EP
years.p: A Drag City EP (No. 81) between Wild Love and The Doctor Came at Dawn.

years.h: The Doctor Came at Dawn, Smog's fifth album
years.p: Bill Callahan's 1996 LP for Drag City (No. 95), the last before he started working with Jim O'Rourke.

years.h: Red Apple Falls: five days with Jim O'Rourke
years.p: Recorded October 30 to November 3, 1996. [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] co-produced and played bass, piano, Hammond, hurdy-gurdy and drums. Folk and country come into Smog.
years.xp: It was the first of two Smog albums O'Rourke produced. Drummer [[Thymme Jones|9a02fbd4-3e27-4c6c-9c72-308832e32820]] of [[Cheer-Accident|5c38924d-13ac-4f50-b81f-773f5f807f56]] played on it too. "Red Apples" was an old song from the 1991 Floating EP.

years.h: Bill Callahan leaves Chan Marshall and drives to Chicago
years.p: Bill Callahan and [[Cat Power|05755bf1-380c-487f-983f-d1a02401fa28]]'s Chan Marshall had been living in a farmhouse in Prosperity, South Carolina. After they split he wrote most of Knock Knock on the drive to Chicago.

q: An engineer, Jim O'Rourke, who liked my music.
years.h: Knock Knock: a string quartet and the Chicago Children's Choir
years.p: Ten days with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]], uncredited, at the desk. The Chicago Children's Choir sings on "No Dancing" and "Hit the Ground Running".
years.xp:
Stereogum reported Bill Callahan stood outside the booth mouthing along as the kids sang. The band included Thymme Jones, Tim Mulvenna of the [[Vandermark 5|c4191da1-6477-4f2a-a218-6bd438e294e3]], [[Liam Hayes|bb2c8e53-ff20-429e-b095-50c39ee0c393]] and guitarist Loren Connors.

The NME ranked it the tenth best album of 1999 and The Independent named it the year's best pop album. "Held" later sold Cadillac Escalades in 2008 ads and was covered by [[Spoon|84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184]] in 2022.

eras.title: A soundtrack cameo and a Peel session
eras.text: Knock Knock made Smog one of the better-known names on Drag City, and Hollywood noticed. Bill Callahan answered with slower, stranger records.

years.h: "Cold Blooded Old Times" lands in High Fidelity
years.p: The Knock Knock single plays in the John Cusack record-store film High Fidelity and on its soundtrack album.

years.h: Dongs of Sevotion, a double LP for Drag City
years.p: Smog's eighth album, more meditative than Knock Knock, with the spoonerism title to match.

years.h: 'Neath the Puke Tree EP remakes a 1990 song
years.p: The Drag City EP re-records "A Jar of Sand" from Sewn to the Sky, ten years on.

years.h: Rain on Lens, Smog's hypnotic ninth album
years.p: AllMusic called it hypnotic. Around here the name starts appearing in brackets, as (Smog).

years.h: Bill Callahan records a Peel session as Smog
years.p: A BBC session for John Peel. Drag City finally released it in 2024 as The Holy Grail.

years.h: Supper, the second-to-last Smog album
years.p: Bill Callahan's 2003 album for Drag City, two years before A River Ain't Too Much to Love.

eras.title: A river, then his own name
eras.text: Bill Callahan moved to Texas, made the Smog album many fans rate highest, and then retired the name. He had wanted to drop it one record earlier.

years.h: Bill Callahan and Joanna Newsom become a couple
years.p: Bill Callahan dates the harpist [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] from 2004 to 2007. She plays piano on the next Smog album and he sings on her record Ys.

years.h: A River Ain't Too Much to Love, cut at Willie Nelson's Texas studio
years.p: Recorded in November 2004 at Pedernales in Spicewood, Texas, with drummer [[Jim White|e1f83b22-d40e-400a-8ebb-4e59b5b53d31]] of [[Dirty Three|af8bb921-4d67-4f0d-ba17-6215315f92e4]], [[Thor Harris|118ca2e9-443a-4933-a436-9c9298472224]] and Joanna Newsom on piano.
years.xp:
Bill Callahan wanted to release it under his own name, and backed off under pressure from Drag City, per Wikipedia. It became the last Smog album. Chloë Sevigny appears in the video for "I Feel Like the Mother of the World".

"I'm New Here" became the title track of [[Gil Scott-Heron|b5b89643-c488-4f39-a302-25cab31084a5]]'s last album, in 2010.
play: A River Ain't Too Much to Love

q: When I changed the name, I felt like it wiped the slate clean.
years.h: Bill Callahan retires Smog with Woke on a Whaleheart
years.p: Woke on a Whaleheart comes out under Bill Callahan's own name. He said Smog was an ugly word for a thing that didn't exist.
years.xp: He later said the Smog name had kept the singer-songwriter tag away from him for a long time, and that dropping it cleaned the slate.

eras.title: Smog songs keep turning up
eras.text: Bill Callahan's solo career outgrew Smog's, but the old songs kept finding new homes, from car ads to Spoon records. Drag City went back into the vaults too.

years.h: "Held" sells Cadillacs
years.p: The Knock Knock song "Held" plays in Cadillac Escalade TV commercials.

years.h: Gil Scott-Heron sings a Smog song on his last album
years.p: [[Gil Scott-Heron|b5b89643-c488-4f39-a302-25cab31084a5]] names his final album, I'm New Here, after his cover of the song from A River Ain't Too Much to Love.

years.h: Spoon cover "Held" on Lucifer on the Sofa
years.p: [[Spoon|84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184]] open their 2022 album with the Knock Knock song.

years.h: Drag City issues Smog's 2001 Peel session as The Holy Grail
years.p: The December 10, 2001 BBC session for John Peel, released 23 years later as a 12-inch EP.

sources.title: Wikipedia: A River Ain't Too Much to Love
